A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3D-GSW work, with matching authors, core pipeline and main experiments. Text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. v3 ends with references; v4 additionally contains supplementary Sections 6–10.

before.justification: v3 reports original comparative experiments, watermark robustness tests and component ablations on Blender, LLFF and Mip-NeRF 360 in Tables 1–6 and Figures 3–8.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds decoder studies, sensitivity analyses, dynamic-scene evaluation and a model-compression failure experiment.

M1.justification: The stated LPIPS loss changes from expected L1 feature differences in v3 Equation 9 to learned layer-weighted squared differences in v4 Equation 13. This is a limited loss-formulation revision; an implementation change is not established. FGD, gradient masking, the LL2 decoder input and the other loss components remain.

E1.justification: v4 extends the static-scene evaluation to six dynamic Neural 3D Video scenes using Spacetime/4D-GS. It also adds Gaussian-cloning attacks and model compression with access to the original training data. MS-COCO is newly identified as decoder-pretraining data, without establishing that the pretraining dataset changed.

E2.justification: The main StegaNeRF, WateRF and without-FGD comparisons remain. Supplementary component comparisons introduce evaluated alternatives such as joint decoder training, pixel/DFT/DCT decoder inputs and FGD using DWT or DCT (Tables 7–8 and 11). These expand the comparison methods within component studies; the dynamic and compression evaluations reuse existing external baselines.

E3.justification: Retained experiments keep their principal datasets, message lengths and training settings. New evaluation designs include watermarked versus unwatermarked controls, transform and hyperparameter sweeps, parameter cosine-similarity measurements, and attack-strength sweeps. Section 10.3 adds 32-bit dynamic-scene evaluation with FVD, while Section 10.4 specifies compression under attacker access to training data.

E4.justification: Beyond v3's component-removal, subband and pruning analyses, v4 investigates decoder memorization, decoder inputs and DWT levels, splitting separately from pruning, alternative FGD transforms, patch size, selection ratio and mask strength. It also adds frequency-domain error analysis, distortion-strength curves and the compression failure case (Tables 7–17; Figures 9–18).

E5.justification: Both versions state in Section 4.1 that experiments use five different seeds. Neither reports confidence intervals, standard deviations, significance tests or statistical error bars. The added tables and plots continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Existing numerical entries in Tables 1–6 are retained. New results include cloning accuracy of 95.99% for 3D-GSW, 82.32% for WateRF and 75.56% for StegaNeRF (Table 3). The new dynamic evaluation reports 97.62% accuracy and FVD 125.98 for 3D-GSW (Table 16); compression yields only 55.51% accuracy (Table 17). Numerous component, sensitivity and per-view results are also added.

T1.justification: The LPIPS definition changes mathematically from an L1 feature difference to a layer-weighted quadratic expression (v3 Equation 9; v4 Equation 13). Other equation edits mainly separate, renumber or compact existing expressions. Supplementary Equation 17 repeats the existing gradient mask; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: FGD, gradient masking and wavelet-subband loss for robust watermarking with high rendering quality and efficiency. Replacing 'state-of-the-art' with 'superior performance' does not materially redefine these claims. Dynamic-scene results add supporting scope in the supplement.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations of decoder memorization, splitting versus Gaussian enlargement, and the trade-offs governing patch selection and mask strength. Most consequentially, Section 10.4 identifies compression with training-data access as a watermark-removal failure condition. This substantially qualifies applicability beyond v3's existing limitation about decoder pretraining, although broad robustness wording remains in the main text.

D1.justification: Section 6.1 newly specifies decoder architecture, MS-COCO pretraining, Adam learning rate, MSE loss weights, distortion layers and PCA whitening. v4 also documents three linear layers for the StegaNeRF adaptation, splitting each selected Gaussian into two, and the compression method used. These substantially expand reproducibility information without establishing corresponding implementation changes. The advertised project-page address also changes.

R1.justification: The main research positioning remains stable. New references support the supplement, including Stable Signature, MS-COCO, Neural 3D Video, Spacetime Gaussian Feature Splatting and Compressed 3D Gaussian Splatting. Section 6 additionally contrasts the pretrained decoder with StegaNeRF's decoding requirements. The duplicated densification reference does not represent a new distinct work.

P1.justification: The main argument and section order remain intact. v4 edits prose in the abstract, introduction and related work, shortens loss names, adds acknowledgements and organizes supplementary material into Sections 6–10. The existing decoder-pretraining limitations paragraph is relocated rather than newly introduced.

P2.justification: v4 adds extensive visual reporting: component-comparison tables, sensitivity and robustness curves, frequency visualizations, dynamic/compression result tables and multi-view image grids (Tables 7–17; Figures 9–27). Table 3 gains a cloning column. Existing main figures are largely retained, with terminology updates and layout changes, including relocation of Table 5.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially fills v3's gaps in decoder-training documentation and support for design choices through unwatermarked-image controls, isolated component studies and attack-strength sweeps. Dynamic-scene evaluation broadens validation, while Table 17 exposes an important compression failure previously unreported. Although the main text still uses broad robustness language, the added evidence and explicit failure boundary substantially improve reproducibility and the assessment of applicability.
